text:
DevBot: CI perf-regress-alert: microbench 'kv_lookup_throughput' exceeded threshold in PR #5439 (delta +12.4%). build: ci-5439-merge-2

maria: saw this when I woke up, thanks for the ping. quick glance at the artifact shows higher tail on long-seq runs (:chain of 1024 tokens).

aj: re-ran locally against commit head, reproduced ~10-13% slower on the KV hotpath. looks like more kernel invocations per token.

tom: interesting — noise on short-seq is fine. long sequences regressed. could be a change in kernel selection fallback ordering in the selector heuristics.

maria: PR touched the kernel selector thresholds and the batch-wait heuristic for latency SLOs. @aj can you dump the kernel selection trace for the failing run?

aj: pasted the short trace below:
```
KERNEL_SELECT: model=redwood-v1, seq_len=1024, batch_size=8
heuristic_score=0.42 -> selected_kernel=generic_attention_32
fallback_chain: optimized_attention_16 -> generic_attention_32
reason: quant_threshold_flip at 0.4
```

aj: looks like the selector flipped the boundary at 0.4; previously that run picked optimized_attention_16 which uses fused kernels. now it prefers generic -> more memcpy + less fused work.

sam: can we force the old kernel for a quick bisect test? try `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=optimized_attention_16` in CI.

aj: kicked a job with that env var — build ci-5439-force-kernel. if perf returns to baseline it's a good sign.

DevBot: re-run finished: ci-5439-force-kernel -> microbench delta -0.8% (within noise). :eyes:

maria: that pretty strongly implicates the selector change. we need a targeted bisect of the selector commit in the PR.

tom: I'll run git bisect across the selector/heuristics edits. quick hypothesis: the change added a hysteresis factor to avoid flapping, but the math inverted an inequality for long sequences.

aj: here's a minimal repro script I used (please run inside docker image redwood/bench:latest):
```
# repro/kv_long_seq.sh
python bench.py --model redwood-v1 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --iters 200 --trace-kernel
```

sam: running that locally shows the same selection flip. if we revert the one-line sign change in heuristics we probably restore perf. but we should add a unit test for kernel selection parity on long seqs.

maria: agreed. we should not revert without a test. BUT this is a rollout blocker for dedicated and private customers — can we hotfix by tightening the decision margin instead of full revert? e.g., restore threshold to 0.45 and add test.

aj: submitted quick PR #5440 that bumps the threshold back and includes a deterministic test for seq_len 1024. request review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/5440

tom: also discovered a small batching heuristic interaction: when batch_wait_ms < 2 the selector is consulted more often causing more kernel churn. not sure if related but noted.

sam: +1 on the small margin change. add changelog note and monitor staging for perf. I'll pin the canary rollout to 0% until CI clears.

DevBot: note: automated canary paused for PR #5439 due to perf alert.

maria: next steps: (1) merge #5440 after 1 review, (2) add CI microbench job that asserts kernel choice for long seqs, (3) backfill a test that exercises batch_wait hysteresis. I'll take ownership.

aj: will follow up with a flamegraph from the failing run to confirm no other hotspots.

tom: if we need an emergency revert, call it out in #incidents and I'll handle the release rollback.

maria: thanks all. keeping this thread for the bisect outcome. please post minimal repro artifacts and links here. :thumbsup:
